questions.prompt: Where does an Angular 20 app start?

options.text: `app.module.ts` declares every component and bootstraps the app

questions.explanation: `main.ts` starts the app with the root component and the app config, which holds the providers. Standalone apps have no `AppModule`.

questions.prompt: What does the last line return?

options.text: `"10 likes"`: a computed value is calculated only once
An error: `label` must be recalculated by hand

questions.explanation: A `computed` signal remembers which signals it read. When `likes` changes, `label` is recalculated the next time someone reads it.

questions.prompt: What happens when you build this?

code.label: like-button.component.ts

options.text: The build fails: a computed signal is read-only and has no `set`
It builds, and `label` shows "0 likes" until `likes` changes
It builds, and `set` also changes `likes` to 0

questions.explanation: `computed` returns a read-only signal. Change the signal it is derived from instead: `this.likes.set(0)`.

questions.prompt: The feed throws an error as soon as it renders the post count. Click the buggy line.

code.label: feed.component.ts

questions.explanation: A `computed` must only read signals. Writing to a signal inside it throws (NG0600). Derive the second value too: `readonly hasPosts = computed(() => this.posts().length > 0);`.

questions.prompt: `PostsApiService` is `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })`. The feed and the profile page both call `inject(PostsApiService)`. How many instances are there?

options.text: One, shared by the whole app
None until it is added to a `providers` array

questions.explanation: `providedIn: 'root'` registers the service in the root injector, so every `inject()` gets the same instance. It is created the first time something asks for it.

questions.prompt: The user opens the app at `/`. Put the steps in order.
items: The browser loads `index.html` and the app's JavaScript
The router matches `/` and shows `FeedPageComponent` in the `<router-outlet>`
questions.explanation: `index.html` only holds the `<app-root>` element. Everything else starts in `main.ts`: the app config sets up the providers, the root component renders, and the router fills the outlet with the page for the URL.
